name: Visual Genome
description: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations
creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bemstein, Li Fei-Fei (Stanford University, Yahoo Inc., Snapchat Inc.)
citeAs: Ranjay Krishna et al., Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations
rai:dataCollection: The Visual Genome dataset was collected using Amazon Mechanical Turk, where crowd workers provided dense annotations of objects, attributes, and relationships within images.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset consists of over 108,000 images sourced from the intersection of YFCC100M and MS-COCO datasets.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data was preprocessed by removing non-alphanumeric characters, lowercasing, and stripping excess whitespace from region descriptions.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd workers were instructed to write descriptions for regions in images, extract objects, attributes, and relationships, and create question-answer pairs based on the images.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 42 region descriptions per image, with an average of 21 objects, 18 attributes, and 18 relationships per image.
rai:annotatorDemographics: 93.02% of workers contributed from the United States, with a near-balanced split of 54.15% male and 45.85% female workers.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is biased towards images of people and may not represent all visual contexts equally.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may contain biases inherent in the source data and is primarily focused on North American contexts.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset can be used for training, testing, validation, and fine-tuning models for visual understanding tasks.
